newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kabila-Tshisekedi meeting likely, Kasavubu says.
newsitem.headline: Kabila-Tshisekedi meeting likely, Kasavubu says.

text.p: Justine Mpoyo Kasavubu, one of only two opposition figures drafted into Laurent Kabila's government in the new Democratic Republic of Congo, said on Monday she expected Kabila to set up a meeting with veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi.

"Now that our enemy (Mobutu) has disappeared I don't see why ...Kabila...would refuse to meet Tshisekedi and I cannot imagine that...Tshisekedi, with the fight he's waged so far, would not recognise Kabila," Kasavubu told a news conference here.
"So I think that those two statesmen will meet," she said.
Kabila's rebel forces drove ailing veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko from power in what was fornerly known as Zaire earlier this month.
Kabila has so far withstood intense domestic pressure and some Western encouragement to appoint Tshisekedi to a key government post such as prime minister.

Public Service Minister Kasavubu, daughter of Zaire's first president Joseph Kasavubu, ran a vociferous anti-Mobutu campaign from Brussels as spokeswoman for Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party.
She is due to return to Kinshasa later this week after 15 years in exile.
